newsitem.title: FINLAND: Markka will join ERM autumn '96, Finmin says - paper.
newsitem.headline: Markka will join ERM autumn '96, Finmin says - paper.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto was on Friday quoted as saying that the government had signalled that the markka will be linked to Europe's exchange rate mechanism this autumn.

"The government has signalled that the link will happen in the autumn," Niinisto said in an interview to be published on Monday in the newsletter of a major central trade union, the Finnish Confederation of Salaried Employees (STTK).
The text of the interview was made available to news media on Friday.
Until now, the government has repeatedly said the decision had yet to be made whether to link the markka to ERM.
"There are strong pressures, and abroad people are asking whether Finland does not dare to join ERM," Niinisto said.
"In my personal opinion, membership of ERM brings more exchange rate stability and supports economic development and credibility," he said.
On Thursday, in a question-and-answer session in parliament, Niinisto said the central issue for the government in deciding on a link was whether a peg would increase monetary stability.
Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said in a newspaper interview on September 27 that the government must decide this autumn whether linking the markka to ERM would increase economic policy credibility.
